utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Hi Dane, I’m glad we’re talking about the repair drive—what still needs sorting out first?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Mara, sorry I’m coming in a bit late as usual. I’d first sort out what items we can actually repair and who’s bringing tools.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: That makes sense—let’s start a simple list of repairable items and tool volunteers so nobody shows up guessing.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Hi Hana, what repairs are we collecting for first?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Hi Leo — before we start collecting, can you confirm which repairs are most urgent and whether anyone has already promised supplies or help?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Most urgent are the loose porch rail and the leaking gutter by Mrs. Park’s place. I haven’t heard of any promised supplies or help yet.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Hi Noah, I’m starting a quick list of what supplies we have for the repair drive—do you know what’s already been collected?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, I’m not totally sure—I might’ve missed the latest drop-off. I think I saw a box of tape and some spare screws by the community room, but Cleo, you may want to double-check me.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Thanks, Noah — I’ll mark tape and spare screws as tentative and swing by the community room to confirm them.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Hi Pia, I heard a little about the repair drive, but not much yet. What are you hoping people can help with?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Mostly I’m hoping people can help with the practical bits—where we’ll set up tables, who’s bringing tools, and how we’ll keep the line from getting chaotic.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That makes sense; maybe I can help by checking in with a few people one-on-one about tools and table space. What’s the most urgent gap right now?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Nell, what exactly needs repairing for the drive, and when do you need people to show up?

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I’m still piecing it together from what folks have told me, but I heard they’re looking at small appliances and bikes mostly. I don’t want to give you the wrong time yet—let me check with the organizers and get back to you.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Alright, please check and tell me today if you can, so I know whether to bring tools or just send folks your way.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh Gus, have you heard when the repair drive is kicking off? I’ve got half the block asking what tools or parts they should bring.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: I haven’t heard the exact kickoff time yet, Tess, but I can swing by the community board and check. Tell folks I’ll bring my tool chest and spare fasteners either way.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’d be perfect, Gus—I'll tell everyone you’re checking the board and bringing the tool chest and fasteners just in case.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Opal, I’m helping spread the word about the repair drive—want me to make sure you’re on the invite list?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Yes, please put me on the invite list, Quinn. Send me the location and time too, and I’ll note it down.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Absolutely, Opal—I’ll add you to the invite list and send over the time and location as soon as I have them.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Kira, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive—how can I pitch in?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Thanks, Sam—but before I count you in, can you confirm what kind of help you’re actually offering: tools, time, supplies, or all of the above?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: I can offer time and tools for sure, and I’m happy to bring a few basic supplies if you tell me what’s most needed.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Bo, I’m glad we’re getting the repair drive moving—do you have a sense of which items neighbors need help with most?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Rosa—mostly small appliances and bikes from what I’ve skimmed, but I haven’t got the full list yet.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s a helpful start, thank you—if you can send me the full list when you have it, I’ll sort it into categories and line up the right volunteers.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Eli, I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—do you know what the plan is yet?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I’ve heard it’s being organized, Vik, but I don’t have the schedule yet. Once they post the time and drop-off details, I’d like to have it all written down clearly.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Got it, Eli—I’ll keep an ear out for the schedule and drop-off details, and once they’re posted I’ll help repeat them around so folks have it clear.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Hi Uli, remind me where we landed on the repair drive? I want to help, but I’ve misplaced the details already.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I think we were gathering small fixes people can’t manage alone—leaky taps, loose steps, that sort of thing. If you want, I can quietly check the notice and tell you where to sign up.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: That would be a kindness, Uli, thank you. If you tell me where to put my name, I’ll write it down before it slips away again.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Ira, I’ve been hearing a lot of neighbors want to help with the repair drive—maybe I can connect a few groups so we’re not all working separately.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That sounds smart, Jules—I’ve heard the same while I’ve been out, and folks seem eager but a little scattered. If you start connecting groups, I can pass along anything useful I hear on my errands.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That’d be perfect, Ira—if you hear who’s got tools, supplies, or time to spare, send them my way and I’ll start matching people up.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Dane, I’m getting the word out about the repair drive today—do you know anyone on your block who might want to bring something by or lend a hand?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: I’m a bit late catching up, but I can ask around my end of the block this afternoon. I know a couple folks with busted lamps or small appliances who might be interested.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: That’d be perfect, Dane—thank you! If you hear back, send them my way and I’ll make sure they’ve got the time and drop-off details.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Hi Eli, I heard a little about the repair drive, but not much yet. What are you hoping neighbors can help with?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I’d like us to keep it simple: list what needs fixing, match folks with the skills or tools, and set one clear Saturday morning to do the work.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That sounds doable. I can ask a few neighbors what they need fixed and what tools they might be willing to lend.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Mara, I’m happy to help with the repair drive—do you know what times you’re thinking? I can work around school drop-off and pickup.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Thanks, Faye—that would be wonderful. I’m thinking late morning, maybe 10 to noon, so it doesn’t bump into school drop-off or pickup.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: That timing works well for me—10 to noon fits neatly between school runs. I can help set up and be there for the whole window.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Vik, I’m glad we’re talking about the repair drive—I know a few folks from different blocks who’d probably love to pitch in. What kind of help do you need most right now?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Honestly, the biggest help right now is spreading the word and getting names of folks who can bring tools, spare parts, or a little time to fix things.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Perfect, I can start a little signup list and pass it around to the Oak Street crew and the parents’ group. I’ll ask who can bring tools, parts, or a couple hours, then get those names back to you.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Pia, I heard you’re organizing the repair drive—if you need extra tools or a spare pair of hands, I’m happy to pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Thanks, Gus—that would help, but I’m still figuring out where we’ll store everything and how to keep sign-ups from getting chaotic.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: No problem—I've got a couple folding tables and labeled bins we can use, and I can help set up a simple sign-up sheet so folks don’t all pile in at once.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Hi Rosa, I’m starting a careful list for the repair drive—who’s bringing what, and where each item should be dropped off.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s perfect, Opal—thank you. I can send you the names I’ve got so far and mark the community room as the main drop-off spot unless we need a second location.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Great, Rosa—send me the names when you can, and I’ll list the community room as the main drop-off for now with a note that a second spot is still undecided.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Hana, what exactly still needs fixing, and who’s already signed up to help?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I don’t want to guess—let me check the repair list and the signup sheet first, then I can tell you exactly what’s left and who’s committed.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Good—check both, and tell me what’s urgent first so we can match people to the right jobs.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Cleo, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive—how can I help get things moving?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Thanks, Sam — could you start by checking who has spare screws, tape, batteries, and basic tools? I’ll make a simple list so we know what we’re missing before the drive.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, I’ll ask around today and note who has screws, tape, batteries, and basic tools so we can see the gaps.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Noah, I’m still catching up from what folks have told me—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, I might be a bit behind too, Nell, but last I heard people were still trying to gather names and figure out what repairs are most urgent.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That’s helpful, thanks—if there’s a list going around, I’d be glad to add my name and ask the few folks I’ve met what they need most.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Wait, can you confirm what exactly the repair drive is for and who’s organizing it?

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh yes—it's a neighborhood repair drive for fixing up small household things, bikes, and appliances instead of tossing them. I heard the community center is organizing it with a few handy volunteers from our block.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Okay, thanks—can you confirm when and where it’s happening before I tell anyone else?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hi Uli, I’ve been out running errands and haven’t heard much yet—how’s the repair drive coming along?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: It’s coming along slowly, I think. A few folks have offered tools and time, so I’m just trying to keep my head down and help where I can.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That’s good to hear—slow is still moving. If you hear where an extra pair of hands is most useful, let me know and I’ll try to swing by after my errands.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Hi Leo—remind me, is the repair drive this weekend? I’d like to help if I haven’t already promised to bring something.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Yes, it’s this weekend. I don’t have you down for anything yet, so helping on the day would be great.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Great, thanks for reminding me, Leo. I’ll come by on the day and help wherever you need an extra pair of hands.
